title: A subsampled hit on the last sample gives a reversed rank range and panics
body:
`Index::rank_range` (`libsufr/src/index.rs`, the `Subsampled` arm) turns a hit on the subsampled suffixes into a range of ranks in the whole suffix array. When the hit is the single last sample, it ends the range at `ranks.len()`, the number of samples, instead of at `len_suffixes`. The range is then reversed or short, and `suffixes_at` panics in `FileAccess::get_range`.

Reproduce with `sufr locate -m 1 data/inputs/1.sufr T`. A sweep at 2632038 and at the step 3 commit found 30 panicking (fixture, flags, query) combinations, the same before and after, so the behavior predates the reorganization. The code carries a TODO at the site.

When a hit spans more than one sample, the range ends at `ranks[last] + 1`, which also cuts off the last group. That may be the same mistake or a second one.
